Ἀβραάμ.long: Abraham, progenitor of the Hebrew race.
Ἀβραάμ.as:
Ἀβραάμ (Heb. אַבְרָהָם), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἄβραμος, -ου; MM, VGT, s.v.),
Abraham (Ge 17:5 al.): Mt 1:1, 2 al.

Ἀβιά.long: Abijah, (a) a king, son of Rehoboam, (b) founder of the eighth class of priests.
Ἀβιά.sd: Abijah, the name of two Israelites
Ἀβιά.as:
Ἀβιά (Heb. אֲבִיָּה, אֲבִיָּהוּ), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀβίας, -α),
Abia, Abijah.
1. Son of Rehoboam (III Ki 14:1): Mt 1:7.
2. A priest of the line of Eleazar (I Ch 24:3, 10): Lk 1:5.†

Ἀβιούδ.long: Abiud, son of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim.

Ἅβελ.long: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain.
Ἅβελ.as:
Ἄβελ, (WH, Ἅ-), ὁ, indecl.
(הֶבֶל),
Abel (Ge 4:2-10): He 11:4, 12:24; αἵμα Ἄ., Mt 23:35, Lk 11:51.†

Ἀβιαθάρ.long: Abiathar, a priest in King David's time.
Ἀβιαθάρ.as:
Ἀβιάθαρ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אֶבְיָתָר),
Abiathar (I Ki 21:1): Mk 2:26.†

αββα.as:
Ἀββά (T, -ᾶ), indecl. (Aram, אַבָּא, emphatic form of אַב = Heb. אָב, father),
used in the phrase Ἀ. ὁ πατήρ, Abba, Father (v. Swete on Mk 14:36): Mk 14:36, Ro 8:15, Ga 4:6.†

Ἀβιληνή.long: the Abilenian territory, the territory of Abila (in Syria), a small principality in the mountains of Damascus.

ἄβυσσος.long: the abyss, unfathomable depth, an especially Jewish conception, the home of the dead and of evil spirits.
ἄβυσσος.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a variation of G1037 (βυθός);
ἄβυσσος.as:
ἄ-βυσσος, -ον
(< Ion. βυσσός = βυθός),
1. in cl., boundless, bottomless (e.g. ἄ. πέλαγος, ἄ. πλοῦτος Æsch.).
2. [In LXX (for תְּהוֹם, Ge 1:2, al.; exc. Is 44:27, Jb 41:22 for צוּלָה, מְצוּלָה, Jb 36:16 for רַחַב) and] NT, as subst. (MM, VGT, s.v.), ἡ ἄ. (sc. χώρα), the abyss;
(a) of the sea (Ge 1:2);
(b) of the underworld, as the abode of the dead: Ro 10:7 (a paraphrase of De 30:13 LXX); as the abode of demons, Lk 8:31, Re 9:1, 2, 11, 11:7, 17:8, 20:1, 3 (Cremer, 2).†

ἀβαρής.long: not burdensome, bringing no weight or oppression upon.
ἀβαρής.der: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G922 (βάρος);
ἀβαρής.as:
* ἀβαρής, -ές
(< βαρός),
without weight; metaph. (MM, VGT, s.v.) not burdensome: II Co 11:9.†

Ἀβαδδών.long: Abaddon, Destroyer (i.e. Destroying Angel) or "place of destruction" (personified).
Ἀβαδδών.as:
Ἀβαδδών (Heb. אֲבַדֹּון, destruction; LXX, ἀπώλεια, only in Wisdom Lit., of the place of the ruined dead: Jb 26:6, 28:22, 31:12, Ps 88:12, Pr 15:11*), indecl.;
in NT, Abaddon, the angel of the Abyss: Re 9:11.†
